q2_gaps: an ACTIVE permission verb with an overt permitter ('The Council permits X to V'): the deontic sections map only modals and passive / participial wordings ('are permitted / allowed / forbidden to V') onto (Permitted e) or the kind-level (permitted <action>), and say nothing about an active permit / allow / authorize clause — so whether it is only an ordinary object-control event (the reading taken) or should additionally carry a (Permitted <complement>) status atom is undecided

whether an inceptive's mandatory (Ongoing <activity>) marker still applies when the inception itself sits inside an unrealized control complement: the control rule strips tense/status from the complement event, yet the Inception rule puts Ongoing on the activity one level down, so the parse asserts a top-level ongoing tending that the sentence never claims occurred
notes: Object-control routing (matrix Theme = the reified complement event, the object controller copied in as that event's Agent, no matrix role for the apprentice, no tense on the complement) and the inception pattern (begin event + Theme activity + Ongoing) both follow the instruction set, as does the no-Name common-noun treatment of the capitalized 'the Council' and the singular-collective no-distribution rule.
